title: Defining the Histopathological Extent of Resection in Glioma: Is there R0 Resection in Glioma Surgery? – HighResection Glio (HiResGlio) – A Pilot Study
summary:
This study investigates whether it is possible, in certain brain tumors (gliomas) that are not located in critical brain regions, to achieve a complete tumor removal similar to the so-called “R0 resection” known from other surgical fields. Until now, surgery has mainly focused on removing the parts of the tumor that show contrast enhancement on MRI scans. However, it is known that tumor cells may also be present in the surrounding brain tissue, even if this appears normal on MRI.
To explore this, small tissue samples will be taken from the tumor margins during surgery and immediately examined by an experienced neuropathologist. The surgeon will receive direct feedback on whether tumor cells are still present or whether healthy tissue has already been reached. This information helps the surgeon decide whether to stop the resection or continue safely.
The aim of this pilot study is to determine whether this approach is feasible and meaningful, and whether it may serve as the basis for a larger trial to evaluate the impact of such resections on patient survival and long-term quality of life.
conditions: Neoplasm of uncertain or unknown behaviour of brain and central nervous system

interventions.name: Non-eloquent gliomas (supramaximal resection + intraoperative histopathological assessment of resection margins)
